{"caption":"A CoWork workflow schematic links execution evidence to model and harness reports, alternating updates, and a subsequent evaluation round.","description":"A text-based workflow diagram inside a rounded green border. A dark-green title bar reads “Report-driven co-evolution | CoWork example.” Beneath it, the task is to process a CSV, preserve row order, and submit a checked output; a note says the traces and report excerpts are synthetic and the update axes alternate across rounds.

Section (a), “Execution evidence and failure attribution,” is a three-column table headed Stage, Trace / artifact, and Diagnostic evidence. S3: “Row-order check skipped; no test output.” Diagnostic: “Required skill exists; policy skips it.” S4: “After restart, trial-results.json is used without opening it.” Diagnostic: “Skill omits retrieval and validation in the new workspace.” Below the table, “LLM Attribution” says to pool scores and traces across development tasks and exclude infrastructure failures.

Two report panels sit side by side. Panel (b), “LLM Report,” says: Target—S3, if it has the most frequent model-attributed failures; Cause—known verification procedure skipped; Request—prioritize S3 practice while retaining adjacent stages and end-to-end tasks. Panel (c), “Harness Report,” says: Gap—no artifact check after workspace restart; Add skill—“Retrieve → open → validate saved output,” with arrows indicating that left-to-right sequence; Recovery—try allowed recovery, then stop and report if the artifact remains unavailable.

Below are two update panels. Panel (d), “Model update | harness frozen,” says to Train using “Fresh rollouts → verified rubric rewards → GRPO,” a left-to-right sequence. Its Gate is a development-score drop of no more than 20% relative to the accepted checkpoint; Reject means restore the accepted checkpoint. Panel (e), “Skill update | model frozen,” says to Test the same tasks and model with and without the edit while tools and execution rules stay fixed. Its Gate requires self-tests and safety, improvement at the target stage, overall gain of at least 5 pp, and no end-to-end regression. Reject means keep the current harness.

At the bottom, a “Next round” strip gives the left-to-right sequence “evaluate retained pair → regenerate reports → alternate update axis.” A closing note says accepted skills shape training and updated models reveal the next skill gap. Pale-green section bars and panel backgrounds organize the content; a thin vertical divider separates the report and update columns. There are no plotted data, icons, checkmarks, or crosses, and no connectors between panels beyond the arrows printed within the process text.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
